evidence.symbol: writes one line per transaction and replays stamped state
evidence.observation: Public acceptance contract for JSONL persistence: JsonlStorage.create writes a header line plus one transaction line per commit (asserted at lines 78-80), and JsonlStorage.open replays committed entries, branch-tip values and usage rows with the stamped seq/timestamp (asserted at lines 83-115). This is the exact round-trip the operate demo reproduces on the tiny fixture: entry replay with seq 1/2 and the pi.branch.tip value at seq 3.

Defines the tiny v4 fixture header shape (v=JSONL_FORMAT_VERSION, kind='header', id, storageVersion=1, createdAt, cwd) that the demo reuses verbatim, including the fixed NOW=1_700_000_000_000 clock (line 10) so the replayed timestamps are deterministic.

evidence.symbol: filters non-context assistant response entries while preserving valid messages
evidence.observation: Public acceptance contract for session projection: buildSessionContext walks message entries linked by id/parentId and emits only context-eligible messages in branch order. The demo applies the same utility to the replayed root->child lineage and gets both user messages back in order.

evidence.symbol: projects branch summaries in branch order
evidence.observation: Shows the projection utility preserves parent-linked branch order across entry types, which is why the demo can sort the replayed fixture entries by seq and feed them straight into buildSessionContext to recover the lineage.

The operated class. create() (59-72) atomically publishes header + initial writes; open() (74-83) reads the header, selects v4 replay, and openV4 replays complete lines through parseJsonlTransaction while truncating a torn tail.
Branch tip is a stored value at namespace 'pi.branch.tip' keyed by branch name. The fixture sets branchTip('main') to 'child' and the replay reads it back as { value: 'child', seq: 3 }.
The projection utility operated in phase 3: takes the replayed entry path, orders it by the commit lineage, and returns the agent messages used as the lineage projection.

claims.claim: JsonlStorage writes one JSONL transaction line per commit and, on reopen, replays entries, branch-tip values and usage with their stamped seq/timestamp, so a committed lineage survives a close/reopen cycle.

buildSessionContext projects a replayed parent-linked entry path into agent messages in branch order, filtering non-context assistant responses, so replayed storage entries can be normalized into conversation lineage.

Operating the real utilities on the supplied tiny fixture yields session ID 'tiny-lineage-fixture', branch 'main' with branch tip 'child' (stored at seq 3), parent relation child.parentId='root' resolving to the root entry (parentId null), and a clean replay of 2 entries at seq 1 and 2 with messageCount 2.

conclusion: The JSONL/session utilities were operated end-to-end on a tiny v4 fixture written and then reopened by the real JsonlStorage implementation. The lineage report is: session ID 'tiny-lineage-fixture'; branch 'main' whose tip is entry 'child' (pi.branch.tip value at seq 3); parent relation child.parentId='root' with root.parentId=null, i.e. a two-node root->child lineage; and replay succeeded, recovering both entries in seq order (seq 1/2, timestamp 1700000000000), messageCount 2, which buildSessionContext then projected back into ['hello root','hello child']. No source, task metadata, lockfile or git configuration was modified; the only added files live under .prale-eval/.
